title: Moloch and the scattering
summary: The Baali elder who favoured patience.

claims.text: Moloch, quieter than Nergal, saw the sleeping ancient Children as tools but feared that waking them would bring disaster, and pressed for slow, hidden schemes.
Moloch’s tongue burned like acid at a touch, and the few who crossed the elder and lived bore the scars.
After Mashkan-shapir fell the Baali scattered across Mesopotamia, southern Arabia and the North African coast, hiding in Sidon and Tripoli, holding Wabar and staying in Ashur on the Tigris.
The D’habi changed allegiance from Nergal to the Baali and serve the bloodline as a revenant family.

title: The curse on the Assamites
summary: How the Baali answered the Assamite purge.

claims.text: In a single week the united Assamites wiped out twelve Baali nests across Arabia and breaking Baali hold over Baghdad, Yathrib, Acre and Sidon.
The Assamites left loaves of unleavened bread after each raid as a signature.
The six mightiest nests gathered over a pit of organs in Damascus and, after months of rites and some two hundred mortal sacrifices, bound the Decani to curse the Assamites of Alamut.
The curse turned the Assamite practice of Amaranth into a ravenous craving that won them fear and hatred rather than thanks for their war.

title: Apostate
summary: A 2-point Merit for Baali of converted blood.

claims.text: Many in the bloodline are not Baali by birth but converts from other lines, or close descendants of converts.
An Apostate may swap Obfuscate or Presence for one Discipline of the ancestral clan; Daimoinon cannot be swapped.
Apostates pass more easily as members of other clans, but can never hold leadership in the bloodline.

title: Infernal and Unholy Aura
summary: Two traits tied to True Faith.

claims.text: Unholy Aura, a 7-point Merit, lets a Baali stand firm against most displays of True Faith because the spiritual stench is so strong.
Infernal Aura, a 3-point Flaw, makes the Baali flee True Faith and lets anyone with True Faith within a mile sense the Baali’s presence and direction.

title: Baali Flaws
summary: Marks and burdens of the infernalists.

claims.text: Lord of Flies, a 2-point Flaw, draws an endless cloud of vermin that never leaves and cannot be dispersed.
Carrion Comfort, a 3-point Flaw, means feeding only on cold blood from corpses, gaining one Blood Point fewer than normal each time.
Touched from Beyond, a 1 to 4 point Flaw, brings Devil’s marks such as stench, warty hide or useless extra limbs that can be hidden but never removed, on top of any marks from demonic Investments.

title: Glimpse the Gulf Beyond
summary: A Daimoinon power that cracks open reality.

claims.text: The Baali spends a Willpower point and rolls Stamina + Occult at difficulty 7 against the target’s Willpower at difficulty 7.
One net success costs the target a Willpower point and a die on all rolls for the scene; two bring a Rotschreck check; three risk unconsciousness; four risk an hour of catatonia.
Five or more may leave the target permanently witless unless a Willpower roll succeeds, and Willpower driven to zero can leave a Derangement.

title: The Sleepers stir
summary: Baali fears about the waking of the ancient Children.

claims.text: Many old Baali orders have left the Levant for Europe or the far East, though the land between the Tigris and Euphrates remains their true home.
Too many true names have leaked into the world, bringing the Sleepers nearer to waking than at any time since the first tribe.
Strange plagues are taken as proof that Namtaru is waking, and the others are feared to follow; some Baali seek the oldest true names to control them, others hope worship will spare them.
In Europe, young members of the bloodline who call themselves Mephisto shout names that echo between worlds in their ignorance.

title: Ma-ri-ah
summary: A solitary Baali in Byzantine politics.

claims.text: Ma-ri-ah, called Mary, has turned toward Byzantium and its fragile ties with the Western Church.
Some call this elder a traitor who destroyed the sire; others say Ma-ri-ah is no Baali but an agent of the Setites or Tremere.
A fragment of an Eblaite tablet claims Ma-ri-ah has risen beyond mortal and Cainite limits to become a dark, hungry goddess in flesh.
